messages:
eli_support: FYI customer acme-inc (acct: ACME-237) opened an escalation — intermittent streaming failures. They see a client-side broken pipe ~2s after first chunk and our gateway returns 502/gateway_error. They claim tokens during the attempt were billed as 5xx. Attaching truncated logs below.

eli_support: LOG:
```
[2026-06-02T14:03:12Z] gateway: request_id=req_0a1b2c upstream: read error: upstream prematurely closed connection
[2026-06-02T14:03:12Z] proxy: 502 from upstream, client aborted? errno=104 (Connection reset by peer)
```

mike_sre: @eli_support can you paste the request_id and sample curl (with sensitive fields redacted)? also which client lib/version?

eli_support: request_id=req_0a1b2c, customer sent this simplified repro (using node-fetch via a browser proxy but reproduced with curl):
```bash
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \ 
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \ 
  -d $'4\nTest\n0\n' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
They say if they drop the client socket within 1-3s we sometimes show 502 and it increments 5xx counters.

ana_eng: thanks. two quick hypotheses: 1) client-initiated FIN gets handled by proxy but our metric pipeline marks the request as upstream_failure (-> 5xx) before we classify it as client_abort; 2) chunked-encoding framing + client half-close race where kernel returns ECONNRESET/EPIPE and we treat as upstream close.

ana_eng: can you capture a tcpdump on the gateway host for the request_id window and check for FIN/ACK from client vs RST? quick tcpdump: `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/stream-repro.pcap host <client_ip> and port 443`

mike_sre: also check our gateway logs for "client closed connection" vs "upstream closed" traces. add `--trace` on the gateway and grep for req_0a1b2c. If we see client FIN followed by our upstream handler marking upstream_error, that's likely misclassification.

eli_support: captured pcap and a short trace, attaching snippet: 
```
14:03:11.123 IP client > gateway: Flags [F.], seq 12345 ack 67890 win 0 
14:03:11.124 IP gateway > backend: RST, ack 67891 seq 22222 
```
seems like client FIN then gateway resets backend. customer repro steps: open streaming call, start reading chunks, then kill the browser tab -> broken pipe. They insist it shouldn't bill them for 5xx tokens.

ops_maya: billing impact noted. If the root cause is client-initiated abort, we should not count tokens as 5xx. please attach the full gateway trace and the billing event ids so finance can vet. I'll start a billing escalation ticket with finance and legal. :eyes: @julia_product

julia_product: +1 on refunding credits while we investigate. if we detect a systematic miscount we should proactively credit affected customers. File a ticket with matched request_ids and customer ids. Also need list of affected timestamps.

matt_runtime: quick tactical fix idea: change EOF heuristic to prefer client_abort when we see FIN before upstream EOF within 50ms window. we already have a similar guard for websocket-close. I can push a canary that tweaks the window and adds metric `stream.client_disconnect_cause` (values: client_fin, client_rst, upstream_close, protocol_error).

matt_runtime: repro script to simulate client-abort (run on a test client):
```bash
# open stream and then kill client to simulate FIN
python -c "import requests, time; r=requests.post('https://canary.gateway/v1/stream', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer x'}, data='4\nping\n0\n', stream=True); time.sleep(0.5); exit(0)"
# or: curl -N ... & sleep 0.5; kill -9 $!
```

ana_eng: if we push the canary we should run the repro script in loop and assert `stream.client_disconnect_cause==client_fin` and that billing metric `requests.5xx_billed` does not increment for those request_ids.

eli_support: i've collected ~18 request_ids from the customer window and attached them to the support ticket (TICKET-4521). will upload pcap, gateway trace, and sample billing events.

ops_maya: created billing case FIN-2047 and CC'd finance. tagging as high-priority. please add a short note to the support ticket about timeline and affected credits.

mike_sre: assign me and @matt_runtime to follow the canary results. i'll run repro at scale from different client libs (python/ts/browser) to confirm.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: runtime/stream-eof-heuristic tweak -> canary group=5% at 2026-06-02T20:00:00Z by matt_runtime

eli_support: thanks all. keeping customer updated: offered temporary credit until we confirm the classification. will await canary metrics and then propose full refund if miscount confirmed. :thumbsup:
